description: Divide each album's total Bytes by its total Milliseconds to get the album rate. This makes longer tracks count for more.

c.request: For each album (tracks with no album id count as one group), what's its bytes-per-millisecond rate (from `Bytes` and `Milliseconds`, ignoring missing sizes) and how many tracks does it have? Take the mean of those album rates across all albums. For the albums that come in above that mean, give me one row with their average rate, their average track count, and how far above the mean their rates are on average. No rounding. Divide each album's total Bytes by its total Milliseconds to get the album rate. This makes longer tracks count for more.
c.sql:
WITH album_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    AlbumId,
    SUM(Bytes) * 1.0 / SUM(Milliseconds) AS rate,
    COUNT(*) AS track_count
  FROM Track
  WHERE Bytes IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY AlbumId
),
mean_rate_calc AS (
  SELECT AVG(rate) AS mean_rate
  FROM album_stats
),
above_mean AS (
  SELECT 
    a.rate,
    a.track_count,
    a.rate - m.mean_rate AS above_mean_amount
  FROM album_stats a
  CROSS JOIN mean_rate_calc m
  WHERE a.rate > m.mean_rate
)
SELECT 
  AVG(rate) AS average_rate,
  AVG(track_count) AS average_track_count,
  AVG(above_mean_amount) AS average_above_mean
FROM above_mean;

b.request: For each album (grouping tracks with NULL AlbumId separately), calculate the album's bytes-per-millisecond rate as the sum of all non-NULL bytes divided by the sum of all milliseconds, count its total tracks, compute the mean rate across all albums, then return one row containing: the mean rate of albums above the overall mean, the mean track count of those above-mean albums, and the average amount by which those above-mean album rates exceed the overall mean rate.
b.sql: WITH album_metrics AS (SELECT AlbumId, SUM(CASE WHEN Bytes IS NOT NULL THEN Bytes ELSE 0 END) as total_bytes, SUM(Milliseconds) as total_milliseconds, COUNT(*) as track_count, CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN Bytes IS NOT NULL THEN Bytes ELSE 0 END) AS FLOAT) / CAST(SUM(Milliseconds) AS FLOAT) as bytes_per_ms FROM Track GROUP BY AlbumId), mean_rate AS (SELECT AVG(bytes_per_ms) as mean_bytes_per_ms FROM album_metrics), above_mean_albums AS (SELECT am.bytes_per_ms, am.track_count, am.bytes_per_ms - mr.mean_bytes_per_ms as excess_rate FROM album_metrics am CROSS JOIN mean_rate mr WHERE am.bytes_per_ms > mr.mean_bytes_per_ms) SELECT AVG(bytes_per_ms) as mean_rate_above_mean, AVG(track_count) as mean_track_count_above_mean, AVG(excess_rate) as avg_excess_rate FROM above_mean_albums
b.raw: For each album (grouping tracks with NULL AlbumId separately), calculate the album's bytes-per-millisecond rate as the sum of all non-NULL bytes divided by the sum of all milliseconds, count its total tracks, compute the mean rate across all albums, then return one row containing: the mean rate of albums above the overall mean, the mean track count of those above-mean albums, and the average amount by which those above-mean album rates exceed the overall mean rate.

a.request: For each album (tracks with no album id count as one group), work out its rate as the album's total `Bytes` divided by its total `Milliseconds`, ignoring missing sizes, along with how many tracks it has. Then take the mean of these album rates over all albums. Looking only at albums whose rate is above that mean, give me a single row with the average of their rates, the average of their track counts, and the average amount by which their rates exceed the mean. Don't round anything.
a.sql:
WITH album_stats_with_bytes AS (
  SELECT
    AlbumId,
    SUM(Bytes) as total_bytes,
    SUM(Milliseconds) as total_milliseconds
  FROM Track
  WHERE Bytes IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY AlbumId
),
all_track_counts AS (
  SELECT
    AlbumId,
    COUNT(*) as track_count
  FROM Track
  GROUP BY AlbumId
),
album_rates AS (
  SELECT
    s.AlbumId,
    CAST(s.total_bytes AS FLOAT) / CAST(s.total_milliseconds AS FLOAT) as rate,
    t.track_count
  FROM album_stats_with_bytes s
  INNER JOIN all_track_counts t ON s.AlbumId = t.AlbumId
),
mean_rate AS (
  SELECT AVG(rate) as mean_rate
  FROM album_rates
),
above_mean AS (
  SELECT 
    ar.rate,
    ar.track_count,
    ar.rate - m.mean_rate as excess
  FROM album_rates ar
  CROSS JOIN mean_rate m
  WHERE ar.rate > m.mean_rate
)
SELECT
  AVG(rate) as avg_rate,
  AVG(track_count) as avg_track_count,
  AVG(excess) as avg_excess
FROM above_mean

d.request: Compute each album's rate as (total bytes)/(total milliseconds) excluding NULL bytes, count its tracks, find the mean album rate, filter to above-mean albums, return their average rate, average track count, and average excess above the mean.
d.sql:
WITH album_stats AS (
  SELECT
    AlbumId,
    COUNT(*) as track_count,
    SUM(CASE WHEN Bytes IS NOT NULL THEN Bytes ELSE 0 END) as total_bytes,
    SUM(CASE WHEN Bytes IS NOT NULL THEN Milliseconds ELSE 0 END) as total_milliseconds
  FROM Track
  GROUP BY AlbumId
),
album_rates AS (
  SELECT
    track_count,
    CASE WHEN total_milliseconds > 0 THEN total_bytes / total_milliseconds ELSE NULL END as rate
  FROM album_stats
),
mean_rate AS (
  SELECT AVG(rate) as mean_album_rate
  FROM album_rates
  WHERE rate IS NOT NULL
),
above_mean AS (
  SELECT
    rate,
    track_count,
    (rate - mr.mean_album_rate) as excess
  FROM album_rates ar
  CROSS JOIN mean_rate mr
  WHERE ar.rate IS NOT NULL AND ar.rate > mr.mean_album_rate
)
SELECT
  AVG(rate) as avg_rate,
  AVG(track_count) as avg_track_count,
  AVG(excess) as avg_excess
FROM above_mean
